No, the Pentagon is the Pentagon. The slush fund you're thinking of was called the Merged Account. Up until the Anti-Deficiency Act of 1990, what would happen is, whenever a department would come in under budget, they would just dump the remainder into the M Account. Then, if they needed some extra cash, they would just pull it from the M Account. And there was always enough extra cash.

Then, at the Fall Review hearing in 1989, A congressman asked:

You were appropriated $20M for procurement, and then I see that you procured [weapon system], which cost $21M. How did you manage that?

In response, the Under Secretary of Defense turned to his aid for support. She stood up and proudly proclaimed:

We just took it from the M account.

Nobody outside the department had ever heard of this, and suddenly Congress was aware of an account with who knows how many millions just sitting there. Can't have that! So, they passed the ADA in the following year that prescribed they perfect-on-paper-but-terrible-in-practice budget system we have now.

And this was right around the time that the CIA started peddling street drugs. This was to drum up the cash that they no longer had access to in their pet slush fund.
